hypothesis: On an independently estimated (largely molecular) tree of life, each class of animals and plants as recognised in 1859 forms a group of single origin: the most parsimonious reconstruction of class membership on the tree requires only one origin of the class (with any number of losses to nested groups), not several independent origins.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: for 22 classes as circumscribed in the Cuvier/Owen system current in 1859, each represented by 3-7 fixed modern taxa, an induced subtree of the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree is obtained. For each class, membership is coded on the tips and reconstructed by weighted parsimony (gain cost 2, loss cost 1; among equally cheap reconstructions the one with fewest gains); the number of origins = gains + 1 if the root is reconstructed as a member. A class is 'of single descent' if origins = 1. SUPPORTS if at least 80% of the classes (>= 18 of 22) are of single descent.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: REFUTES if 50% or fewer of the classes (<= 11 of 22) are of single descent. Between 12 and 17 is MIXED. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 85% of the representative taxa can be placed as tips, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable). The Dollo count (number of maximal all-member clades) is recorded as a secondary descriptive statistic.
interpretation: Darwin's 'class' is read as the classes his contemporaries used (Cuvier's Règne animal as modified by Owen and Milne-Edwards; de Candolle's three plant classes), not modern monophyletic classes, because the claim says descent embraces 'all the members of the same class' as then delimited: Pisces include cyclostomes, Reptilia include turtles, crocodiles, lizards and snakes but not birds, Acephala include bivalves and tunicates, Insecta include myriapods, Echinodermata include sipunculans and priapulids, Entozoa unite parasitic worms, Acalephae unite jellyfish and comb jellies, Polypi unite corals, hydroids, bryozoans and sponges, Infusoria unite ciliates, flagellates, rotifers and diatoms, Dicotyledones include gymnosperms, and Acotyledones unite ferns, mosses, algae and fungi. 'Embraced by descent with modification' is read as single origin on the genealogy: a paraphyletic class (one origin, nested classes 'lost' from it, e.g. Reptilia relative to Aves) counts as embraced, a polyphyletic class (several origins) does not. Representatives are fixed in advance; the 'independently estimated' genealogy is the Open Tree synthetic tree whose backbone comes mostly from molecular studies.
